articles.title: Timure was a bustling border hub. In hours, the floods wiped it off the map
articles.summary: Heavy floods devastated Timure, a once‑busy border settlement in Nepal, wiping out more than 250 houses and other structures within hours. Only six houses remain partially damaged, and hundreds of residents are still missing or unaccounted for. The disaster has turned the thriving hub into a near‑ghost town, highlighting the severe impact of sudden flooding in the region.

articles.title: War-damaged Gaza building collapses killing 12 people seeking shelter inside
articles.summary: A war‑damaged building in the Gaza Strip collapsed, killing 12 people who were seeking shelter inside. The incident highlights the ongoing danger for families living in thousands of partially damaged structures across the enclave, with hundreds more at risk of similar collapses.

articles.title: Understand Ed Sheeran concert controversy in five points
articles.summary: A controversy erupted during Ed Sheeran's U.S. tour after political statements made by the singer led to the removal of all scheduled opening acts. The dispute has sparked debate over the boundaries of political expression at large-scale concerts, with promoters and venues weighing the balance between artistic freedom and audience expectations. Critics argue the decision suppresses free speech, while supporters claim it protects the concert experience from divisive politics. The incident has drawn attention from media and fans alike, highlighting the growing tension between entertainers and political discourse in live events.

articles.title: Nepal begins a nationwide butterfly count
articles.summary: More than 100 volunteers have launched a nationwide butterfly count across 25 sites in Nepal, aiming to document species diversity, population numbers, and habitat conditions. The citizen‑science effort supports researchers in gathering comprehensive biodiversity data, which is currently limited. By involving local communities, the project seeks to improve understanding of Nepal’s butterfly fauna and inform conservation strategies.

articles.title: Three bodies recovered from flood-hit Chilime hydropower project three weeks later
articles.summary: Three bodies have been recovered from a tunnel at the Chilime hydropower project, three weeks after the devastating floods that struck on August 26. Rescue teams continue to search for additional victims as the disaster's impact remains evident. The recovery underscores ongoing relief efforts and the lingering trauma for affected communities.

articles.title: From hallucinating AI chatbots to wiping out humanity: How did we get here?
articles.summary: The article discusses the risks of AI becoming self-improving and potentially wiping out humanity.

articles.title: How hydro-diplomacy can save the Himalayas
articles.summary: The article discusses how hydro‑diplomacy—cooperation on water data sharing, dam safety standards, and joint management of trans‑boundary rivers—can transform the Himalayan region’s shared water risks into collective resilience. It highlights the need for Nepal, India, China, Bhutan and other riparian states to collaborate on climate‑induced water challenges, improve safety of existing and planned dams, and establish transparent data exchanges. By aligning policies and investing in joint monitoring, the region can protect ecosystems, safeguard downstream communities, and turn potential conflicts over water resources into opportunities for sustainable development.

articles.title: Five bodies recovered from flood-hit Chilime hydropower project
articles.summary: Rescuers searching the tunnels of the Chilime hydropower project in Nepal have recovered five bodies of people missing since the severe floods that struck on August 26. The recovery highlights the ongoing challenges faced by authorities in locating victims and assessing damage after the flood disaster that impacted the hydropower facility and surrounding communities.

articles.title: Five bodies found in flood-damaged Upper Trishuli-1 tunnel
articles.summary: Five bodies have been recovered from the flood‑damaged Upper Trishuli‑1 tunnel, a hydropower project in Rasuwa district, three weeks after severe floods struck the area and left workers missing. The discovery highlights ongoing concerns about safety and rescue operations at the site, where the disaster caused extensive damage to infrastructure and raised questions about emergency response and future project viability.

articles.title: Nepal presses Malaysia to convene joint talks over migrant worker recruitment system
articles.summary: Kathmandu is urging Malaysia to hold an early meeting of a bilateral technical committee after Kuala Lumpur unilaterally selected recruitment agencies for Nepali migrant workers, raising concerns over transparency and fair competition in the recruitment system.

articles.title: Families of missing foreign nationals want answers Nepal can’t give
articles.summary: Families of foreign nationals who have gone missing in Nepal are demanding clearer information, official confirmation of their relatives' status, and assistance with cross‑border searches. Hundreds of foreigners remain unaccounted for, and the government has been unable or unwilling to provide definitive answers, prompting frustration and calls for greater transparency and international cooperation.

articles.title: Deuba loses support as Nepali Congress factions realign
articles.summary: Nepali Congress factions are realigning, with the Thapa-led Congress scheduling its 15th general convention for October 2-5, while Deuba faction has its convention scheduled for December 7-9.

articles.title: Sudurpaschim set to get cable car in its largest private-sector project
articles.summary: The Rs7 billion Jalpa Devi Cable Car, the largest private‑sector project in Sudurpaschim, is slated to start operations in November. The cable car will connect Chisapani with Rajkanda across the Chure hills, creating a new tourism hub in far‑western Nepal and boosting local economic activity.

articles.title: Supreme Court puts controversial parliamentary rules on hold
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has placed two provisions of the House of Representatives' rules on hold, citing potential conflicts with constitutional safeguards regarding constitutional amendments and the authority of existing laws.

articles.title: Ideology is not dead in Nepal. It only changed its address
articles.summary: The article argues that ideology in Nepal is not extinct but has merely moved to a new arena. Over the past fifteen years, the country's political elite have cultivated a deep distrust of grand visions and transformative agendas, creating a vacuum in public discourse. This lack of ideological direction, the author contends, is now manifesting in political stagnation and societal challenges. By highlighting the shift in how ideas are framed and debated, the piece calls for a revival of substantive ideological debate to steer Nepal out of its current impasse.

articles.title: How Nepal can reshape global response to climate catastrophes
articles.summary: The article argues that Nepal, uniquely positioned with both moral authority derived from its vulnerability to climate change and heightened political visibility on the world stage, can become a catalyst for reshaping the global response to climate catastrophes. It examines how Nepal’s experience with glacial melt, landslides, and flood risks gives it credibility, while its active participation in international forums such as the UN Climate Conferences amplifies its voice. The piece calls for Nepal to propose concrete frameworks—ranging from climate‑resilient infrastructure models to community‑based early warning systems—that other nations can adopt, thereby turning its challenges into leadership opportunities in the fight against climate emergencies.

articles.title: Resolve legal hurdles to relief and property rights for families of the missing
articles.summary: The article highlights the legal obstacles that families of missing persons in Nepal encounter when seeking relief and asserting property rights. It argues that existing laws and bureaucratic procedures impede timely assistance, leaving families vulnerable and uncertain about inheritance and compensation. The piece calls on the government to promptly address these barriers through legislative reforms and clearer guidelines, ensuring that the rights of the missing and their relatives are protected.

articles.title: Prithvi Highway blockage ends Thursday as Krishnabhir link restored
articles.summary: The blockage on Nepal's Prithvi Highway was cleared on Thursday after the Krishnabhir link was restored. Authorities have opened a new temporary track over the damaged section, allowing two‑way traffic to resume while work continues to stabilize the main route. The reopening eases travel for commuters and transporters, reducing delays and supporting regional connectivity.

articles.title: Nepal’s wetlands are under pressure. Migratory birds are losing safe havens
articles.summary: Wetlands across Nepal are facing increasing pressure from development, pollution, and climate change, leading to a noticeable decline in migratory bird populations and species diversity. The degradation threatens the vital migration corridor that connects Nepal's wetlands with breeding and wintering grounds throughout Asia, jeopardizing the ecological balance and the livelihoods of communities that depend on these habitats.

articles.title: Nuwakot substation destruction disrupts evacuation of 176.1 MW
articles.summary: The Nepal Electricity Authority reported that the destruction of the Nuwakot substation has halted the evacuation of 176.1 MW of power. The loss is expected to strain the national grid during the upcoming winter season, complicating load management and potentially leading to supply shortages. Authorities are assessing the damage and seeking alternative routes to stabilize the grid.

articles.title: The lonely grind of Nepal’s para powerlifters
articles.summary: Rajani Rai and Pawan Gharti Magar, Nepal's only para powerlifters, train on a single shared bench while self‑funding their diets and equipment. Despite facing physical challenges and a lack of institutional support, they remain determined to represent Nepal at the upcoming 5th Asian Para Games. Their story highlights the broader neglect of para athletes in the country, with minimal funding, inadequate facilities, and limited recognition from sports authorities. Yet their perseverance underscores a growing desire for inclusion and the potential of disabled athletes to excel on the international stage if given proper resources.

articles.title: Booktalk: Tika Prasad Dhakal on the 1923 treaty, Nepal’s independence and the craft of diplomacy
articles.summary: In a recent Booktalk interview, editor Tika Prasad Dhakal reflects on his newly published book ‘State and Craft’, focusing on the 1923 Nepal‑Britain treaty. He examines the treaty’s historical significance in Nepal’s diplomatic evolution, its role in affirming Nepal’s de‑facto independence, and the lessons it offers for contemporary foreign policy. Dhakal argues that understanding the craft of diplomacy demonstrated in the treaty can help Nepal safeguard its national interests amid current geopolitical challenges.

articles.title: Climate change likely to have helped trigger Nepal glacier collapse, scientists say
articles.summary: Scientists say that rising temperatures, thinning glaciers, thawing permafrost and excess meltwater likely created the conditions that led to the late‑August collapse of a glacier in Nepal. The research links the event to climate change, noting that warming trends have accelerated glacier melt and destabilised ice structures. The findings underscore the growing risk of similar incidents in the Himalayas as global warming continues, raising concerns for downstream communities and water resources.

articles.title: Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle reaches New Delhi
articles.summary: Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle arrived in New Delhi to meet Indian counterparts and business leaders, focusing on reconstruction efforts and broader economic cooperation between Nepal and India.

articles.title: Krishnabhir road reopens on Thursday
articles.summary: After being closed for 18 days due to flood damage, the Krishnabhir road has reopened. A newly cut track above the damaged section now allows traffic to flow in both directions, restoring connectivity for local commuters and easing transport disruptions in the area.
